# R5 fifth-chamber f=8: 14-state exact joint certificate

Date: 2026-11-18 (Asia/Shanghai). Proof status: AUTHOR_PROVED / EXACT_FINITE_CHECKED / NOT_REVIEWED.

## Frozen model and statement

Scientific pin 435e77af0d180eac32bd1f9c4c464bc4010b7551; original 101x256 exact integer count table SHA256 50e87f0194cfb3780e84b7bbb6f9a2dca4f79bb4901cab06f1a5b59256fb470b. Physical costs k=214,...,314; normal real reading |y-N_h(k)|<=eta except at most f=8 unmarked arbitrary errors. Let tau=2eta and L=25845652773852463277015040000, U=58182461585441404127941754880.

Consider H14=(18,24,82,34,17,0,1,2,3,144,208,255,50,66).

**Theorem.** For every real L<=tau<U, the exact minimax adaptive cost C8(H14;tau)=8335.

## Proof and executed calculation

The original five-state H0=(18,24,82,34,17) is a subset and has exact cost C8(H0;L)=8335. This gives the entire-chamber lower bound.

For the upper bound, at tau=U-1 construct all inclusion-maximal supports for single normal readings over H14, using only five actual physical costs {214,215,216,223,296}. The fully enumerated masks are in ACTIONS_H14_50_66_RIGHT.txt. The companion C++17 Bellman solver is the previously verified 12-state exact solver extended only to n<=15 (14 counters x4 bits =56 bits in uint64); errors are incremented only while <=8 and saturate at 9, without nibble carry. Exact minimax evaluates all compatible maximal answer supports and returns:

EXACT_RESTRICTED n=14 f=8 V=8335 states=9280321 actions=5

This final exact stdout was produced and stored. The outer command wrapper reported a timeout instead of an independent successful shell-exit receipt, so this evidence is a completed solver output with a wrapper-exit observation limitation. Support masks and compiled source are preserved for rerun.

For any real tau<U, the normal-response compatibility relation is a subset of the one at U-1, since integer centers have integer differences. Thus the upper-bound strategy works throughout the chamber. The upper and H0 lower match.

## Provenance, boundary, and next

This extends the previously published H12 certificate by adding two named configurations 50 and 66 simultaneously. It uses the same scalar observer, not an automatic native P000/X6 provenance-preserving state reduction. It does not assert formal Task/CLAIM/Result/Review acceptance. The complete 256-state f8 question remains bounded by 8335<=C8*<=8343.

Next: test whether a 15th discriminating state forces higher cost under the same five physical budgets, or construct a compact residual-sufficient decomposition for the entire 256-state problem. The prior R5 f8 H12 / four-and-five budget certificates remain at project GitHub commit f4cd0ba590a979165f3360941c9a1651c1f5028c.
